question: A sum of Rs. 600 is lent for 3 years at the rate of 25% per annum. Find the simple interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective simple interest rate for 3 years = 25% × 3 = 75%

Total Interest = 75% of Principal

⇒ SI = (75 ÷ 100) × 600

⇒ SI = 450

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 450.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 600

Rate (R) = 25% per annum

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest (CI)

When interest is compounded annually, Amount = P × (1 + R÷100)T. The Compound Interest is Amount − P.

Difference between CI and SI

For a duration of exactly 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on the same principal is: Difference = P × (R÷100)².

Rule of 72

A widely used mathematical shortcut to estimate the number of years required to double your principal at a given interest rate: Time ≈ 72 ÷ R.
